adds.title: Law 5272 vote of 9 March 2022 - archived 15 March 2022
adds.summary: Guatemala's Congress approved the Law for the Protection of Life and Family on 8 March 2022 to expressly prohibit same-sex marriage in the Civil Code and to prohibit schools from teaching sexual diversity by requiring teaching that heterosexuality is the norm, and after President Alejandro Giammattei requested archiving on 11 March 2022 on grounds it violated the Constitution and international conventions, Congress archived the law with 119 votes, leaving those prohibitions without effect.

adds.title: Codigo de la Ninez y la Juventud (Code on Childhood and Youth) 1997 - repealed 2003
adds.summary: In Guatemala legal gender recognition is not possible and the penal code prohibition of discrimination on grounds including gender does not explicitly cover gender identity, gender expression or sex characteristics with no convictions for discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity grounds recorded through 2021, while attempts to ban educational materials on transgender identities persist alongside normalized conversion practices including by mental health professionals, and despite election of a more progressive government in 2024 Congress remained predominantly conservative with no significant pro-LGBTIQ initiatives and in August 2025 hosted the Meeting for Religious Freedom, Life and Family in Congress to advance an anti-LGBTIQ agenda.

adds.title: Gender identity bill introduced December 2017 - rejected August 2018
adds.summary: On 12 July 2021 Initiative No. 5940 proposing a Law to guarantee the Integral Protection of Children and Adolescents against Gender Identity Disorders was received by the Legislative Directorate and on 13 September 2021 was presented to the plenary of the Congress of Guatemala and assigned to the Human Rights, Education, Science and Technology, and Governance commissions.

adds.title: Bill 5490 advanced December 2021
adds.summary: In December 2021 21 members of Guatemala's congressional Commission on Education, Science and Technology unanimously advanced Bill 5940 to the full Congress where it required three debates and a final vote to become law, proposing on grounds of protecting children from "gender identity disorders" to ban any information about transgender identity from school sex-education curricula and to require media to label transgender content as "not recommended" for under-18s likened to pornography, amid commonplace anti-LGBT violence including the murders of two trans women and one gay man between December 30, 2021 and January 2, 2022 after a bloody 2021 particularly for transgender people, with virtually no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections for LGBT people in place.
